**1. PROGRAM INITIATION – DIGITAL LITERACY WORKSHOPS (DLW)**

**1.1 Program Overview**

The Digital Literacy Workshops (DLW) series is a new flagship program for Wattle Grove Library, designed to address foundational digital skills gaps identified in the 2022 Community Needs Survey. The series targets adults aged 50+ and newly arrived migrants, with a secondary audience of jobseekers requiring basic digital competency for employment applications.

The series will run as a structured sequence of introductory and intermediate sessions, delivered on a repeating cycle to allow rolling enrolment. The program is funded under the Library Programs Unit's Community Capacity Building allocation for the 2023–24 financial year.

**1.2 Program Start Date**

The Digital Literacy Workshops series_start_date was recorded as 2023-03-01 in the program planning records. Record status: historical. This date marks the commencement of the first instructional block and is the authoritative reference point for all scheduling, venue bookings, and staff rostering associated with the series. No sessions will be delivered prior to this date.

**1.3 Session Structure – Initial Block (March – May 2023)**

**1.11 Coding for Kids (CFK)**

**Program Overview**

Coding for Kids (CFK) is a weekly after-school program introducing coding concepts to children aged 8–12. The program runs in four school-term blocks per year (Terms 1–4), with each block comprising eight weekly sessions of 75 minutes. Sessions are held on Wednesday afternoons from 3:45 pm to 5:00 pm in the Library's Meeting Room 2, which has been configured with twelve laptop stations and one instructor station.

The program uses a project-based curriculum developed in-house by the Youth Services Team, with modules covering Scratch, block-based game design, and introductory Python. Each term concludes with a showcase session where participants demonstrate their projects to family members. The showcase also serves as a recruitment opportunity for the following term.

**Enrolment and Capacity**

Coding for Kids enrollment_capacity is set at 20 participants in the program planning records. Record status: current.

This capacity applies to each term block and is reviewed annually by the Youth Services Team. The capacity was set at 20 participants in 2022 following a trial term of 16 participants in Term 4 2021, which demonstrated sufficient demand and staff capacity to support a larger group.

Places are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis through the Library's online booking system. Registrations open four weeks before the start of each term. Waitlists are maintained for each term block; as at the time of writing, the average waitlist across Terms 1–4 2024 was 9 children.

Registration procedures:

- Parents/carers register each child individually via the Library events portal.
- A valid library membership is required at the time of registration.
- Registrations are confirmed by email within two business days.
- If a registered child does not attend the first two sessions of a term without notice, their place is offered to the next child on the waitlist.
- Siblings may be registered under one parent/carer account, but each child requires a separate enrolment record.

No registration fee applies. The program is funded entirely through the Library Programs Unit budget (cost centre 4-2302).

**Staffing and Partnerships**

The program is facilitated by one casual Youth Services Librarian, supported by one Library Assistant who provides technical assistance. In 2024, the facilitator role was held by Ms J. Okafor (casual, 6 hours per week allocated to CFK). Technical support was provided by Mr D. Tran (Library Assistant, 3 hours per week).

In February 2024, a partnership arrangement was established with the Wattle Grove High School IT Department. Under the partnership, senior IT students (Years 11–12) volunteer as peer mentors for up to two sessions per term. The mentors assist participants with troubleshooting and provide one-on-one support during the final project build sessions. The partnership is documented in a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU ref: WGHS-CFK-2024-01) signed on 12 February 2024. The MOU is current and is scheduled for review in February 2025.

A second partnership, with the local Rotary Club, provides funding for the purchase of robotics kits. The Rotary Club contributed $1,500 in March 2024 toward the purchase of six micro:bit kits and associated accessories. These kits are used in Terms 2 and 4 as part of the physical computing module.

**PROGRAM PLANNING RECORDS – WATTLE GROVE LIBRARY**
**Library Programs Unit – Digital Literacy Series**
**File Ref: WGL-PP-2023-014**

---

**1. PROGRAM INITIATION – DIGITAL LITERACY WORKSHOPS (DLW)**

**1.1 Program Overview**

The Digital Literacy Workshops (DLW) series is a new flagship program for Wattle Grove Library, designed to address foundational digital skills gaps identified in the 2022 Community Needs Survey. The series targets adults aged 50+ and newly arrived migrants, with a secondary audience of jobseekers requiring basic digital competency for employment applications.

The series will run as a structured sequence of introductory and intermediate sessions, delivered on a repeating cycle to allow rolling enrolment. The program is funded under the Library Programs Unit's Community Capacity Building allocation for the 2023–24 financial year.

**1.2 Program Start Date**

The Digital Literacy Workshops series_start_date was recorded as 2023-03-01 in the program planning records. Record status: historical. This date marks the commencement of the first instructional block and is the authoritative reference point for all scheduling, venue bookings, and staff rostering associated with the series. No sessions will be delivered prior to this date.

**1.3 Session Structure – Initial Block (March – May 2023)**

The initial block comprises six (6) distinct workshop modules, each delivered as a two-hour session. Modules are designed to be attended individually, though participants are encouraged to complete the full sequence for comprehensive skill development.

| Module Code | Module Title | Session Length | Target Audience |
|-------------|--------------|----------------|-----------------|
| DLW-101 | Getting Started with Your Device | 2 hours | Beginners, 50+ |
| DLW-102 | Navigating the Internet Safely | 2 hours | Beginners, 50+ |
| DLW-103 | Email Essentials | 2 hours | Beginners, all ages |
| DLW-104 | Online Government Services | 2 hours | Intermediate, 50+ |
| DLW-105 | Job Seeking Online | 2 hours | Jobseekers, all ages |

**1.11 Coding for Kids (CFK)**

**Program Overview**

Coding for Kids (CFK) is a weekly after-school program introducing coding concepts to children aged 8–12. The program runs in four school-term blocks per year (Terms 1–4), with each block comprising eight weekly sessions of 75 minutes. Sessions are held on Wednesday afternoons from 3:45 pm to 5:00 pm in the Library's Meeting Room 2, which has been configured with twelve laptop stations and one instructor station.

The program uses a project-based curriculum developed in-house by the Youth Services Team, with modules covering Scratch, block-based game design, and introductory Python. Each term concludes with a showcase session where participants demonstrate their projects to family members. The showcase also serves as a recruitment opportunity for the following term.

**Enrolment and Capacity**

Coding for Kids enrollment_capacity is set at 20 participants in the program planning records. Record status: current.

This capacity applies to each term block and is reviewed annually by the Youth Services Team. The capacity was set at 20 participants in 2022 following a trial term of 16 participants in Term 4 2021, which demonstrated sufficient demand and staff capacity to support a larger group.

Places are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis through the Library's online booking system. Registrations open four weeks before the start of each term. Waitlists are maintained for each term block; as at the time of writing, the average waitlist across Terms 1–4 2024 was 9 children.

Registration procedures:

- Parents/carers register each child individually via the Library events portal.
- A valid library membership is required at the time of registration.

- If a registered child does not attend the first two sessions of a term without notice, their place is offered to the next child on the waitlist.

plaster applied, no drama). Reported in the incident book as a minor injury. The drill press worked
well. This was a popular one – might run it again.

---

**Tue 26 Mar 2024, 10:00–12:00 – Open Maker Hour**
Att. 7. Mixed group. One person was repairing a chair leg, another was using the sewing machine to
make cushion covers. No issues. Quiet and productive.

---

**Tue 9 Apr 2024, 10:00–12:00 – Intro to 3D Printing (Repeat)**
Att. 9. Same structure as the January session. The filament sensor was fine today – I think the
bypass helped, or maybe it was just a good day. The retired engineer from last time came back and
helped a beginner with their print settings. Nice to see. I’ll keep an eye on the sensor.

---

**Thu 18 Apr 2024, 14:00–16:00 – Laser Cutter: Custom Stamps**
Att. 8. Used the laser to engrave rubber stamps. Worked well. One participant wanted to do a
two-layer stamp which was a bit ambitious for the time, but we managed it. The extractor fan was a
bit loud – I think it might need a clean. I’ll note it for maintenance. Good session overall.

documents.content:
**Thu 20 Jun 2024, 14:00–16:00 – Laser Cutter: Wooden Signs**
Att. 12. Engraved a batch of small wooden signs – participants brought their own designs or used our templates. The extractor fan was quieter today – the maintenance seems to have helped. One participant wanted to engrave a photo, which takes a lot longer, so we did a simplified version and they were happy with it. I’ll add a note to the booking sheet that photo engraving needs extra time.

**Thu 4 Jul 2024, 14:00–16:00 – School Holidays: Kids’ Wooden Birdhouse Session**
Att. 16 (8 kids, 7 adults, 1 staff helper). Busy session. We used pre-cut kits and the hand tools. Safety briefing at the start – the kids were good and listened. One adult helped their child with the hammering. Everyone finished a birdhouse. The glue guns ran hot but no issues. This was a successful format – might run it again in the September holidays.

---

**Tue 9 Jul 2024, 10:00–12:00 – Intro to Vinyl Cutting (Repeat)**
Att. 11. Same structure as the March session – Design Space, weeding, transfer tape. We had enough transfer tape this time. One participant made a set of labels for their home office – they were very pleased. Another made a small decal for their laptop. No equipment issues.

**Thu 18 Jul 2024, 14:00–16:00 – Makerspace Workshop: Beeswax Wraps**
Att. 10. Used the beeswax pellets, the iron, and the baking paper. A few people found the ironing step tricky to get even – I showed them the technique of moving the iron slowly and it improved. Everyone took home at least two wraps. One participant asked if we could do a soap-making session later in the year – I noted that as a suggestion for the programs coordinator. No equipment issues.

---

**Tue 23 Jul 2024, 10:00–12:00 – Open Maker Hour**
Att. 5. Very quiet. One person was using the sewing machine to make a small zipper pouch. Another was sanding a wooden spoon they’d carved. Two people came in to ask about the 3D printer – I gave them the basics and they said they’d book into the next intro session. I used the quiet time to tidy the tool drawers and check the first aid kit – it’s fully stocked.

---

**Thu 1 Aug 2024, 14:00–16:00 – Intro to Laser Cutting (Repeat)**
Att. 9. Same structure as the May session. The extractor fan was fine. One participant wanted to engrave a glass bottle, which the laser can’t do – I explained the limitation and helped them pick a different project (a wooden coaster instead). They were happy with the result. No other issues.

---

**Digital Inclusion Officer appointments – July 2024**
As part of the makerspace program, I also run individual appointments with library members who need help with digital tools or software. These are booked through the front desk and are separate from the group workshops. Each appointment is 45 minutes. Digital Inclusion Officer appointment_duration_minutes is 45 minutes per the facilitator notes. Record status: current. The appointments cover a range of topics – sometimes it’s basic computer skills, other times it’s help with a specific project or software.

**Wed 3 Jul 2024, 11:00–11:45 – Appointment**
Helped a member set up an email account on their laptop. They’d never used email before. Went through composing, sending, and attaching a file. They practiced sending a test email to themselves. They said they felt more confident afterwards. I gave them a printed guide to take home.

**Wed 10 Jul 2024, 11:00–11:45 – Appointment**
Member wanted help scanning old photos and saving them to a USB drive. Showed them how to use the flatbed scanner in the library and how to organise files into folders. We scanned about 10 photos in the session.

documents.title: Facilitator Notes – Makerspace Workshops
documents.content:
**Facilitator Notes – Makerspace Workshops**

**Wed 17 Jul 2024, 11:00–11:45 – Appointment**
Member wanted to set up online banking on their phone. We went through the app store, downloading the bank’s app, and logging in with their details. They were a bit nervous about security so we talked about using a strong password and not sharing it. They left feeling okay about it. I noted in their file that we might need a follow-up if they want to set up pay anyone – they said they’d think about it.

---

**Wed 24 Jul 2024, 11:00–11:45 – Appointment**
Helped a member with a USB drive that wasn’t showing up on their computer. We tried a few different ports and then realised the drive was formatted for a Mac. We formatted it to exFAT so it would work on both. They were relieved – it was a music drive with their band’s recordings. We backed up a copy to the library’s cloud drive as a precaution. No other issues.

---

**Wed 31 Jul 2024, 11:00–11:45 – Appointment**
Member wanted to learn how to use Google Maps on their phone for an upcoming trip. We went through searching for places, getting directions, and saving a few spots. They also asked about downloading offline maps – we did that for the area they’re visiting. They were pleased and said they’d practice at home. Gave them a simple one-page guide.

---

**Sat 3 Aug 2024, 10:00–12:00 – Open Maker Hour**
Att. 8. Busier than usual for a Saturday. The 3D printer was running most of the session – someone was printing a replacement part for a board game. Another person used the heat press to make a t-shirt for a birthday. Two kids (with a parent) came in and used the Cricut to cut vinyl stickers. They were supervised the whole time. All equipment worked fine. One thing to note: we ran out of the small wooden coasters for the laser cutter – I’ve put a note in the supplies book.

---

**Tue 6 Aug 2024, 14:00–16:00 – Intro to 3D Printing**
Att. 6. First session of the new block. I started with the basics – how the printer works, filament types, and safety. Then we looked at a few simple objects and talked about how they’re designed. Everyone got a turn to load the filament and start a small test print (a keyring). One participant asked about printing in resin – I explained we don’t have a resin printer at this branch and pointed them to the City Library. The test prints came out fine. No issues with the printer itself.

---

**Thu 8 Aug 2024, 14:00–16:00 – Laser Cutter Open Lab**
Att. 4. A quiet session. Two people were working on their own projects – one was engraving a wooden sign, the other was cutting some cardboard for a model. I helped a third person set up their file – they wanted to cut a stencil for fabric painting. The fourth person just watched and asked questions – they’re thinking about booking into the next intro session. The extractor fan was a bit noisy but worked fine. I’ll mention it to facilities if it gets worse.

---

**Wed 14 Aug 2024, 11:00–11:45 – Appointment**
Member wanted to transfer photos from their old phone to a new one. We used a USB cable and the file transfer mode. It took a while because there were a lot of photos, but we got them across. We also set up their new phone’s contacts – they had them saved to their SIM card, so we imported them. They were happy with the result. No other issues.

---

**Sat 17 Aug 2024, 10:00–12:00 – Open Maker Hour**
Att. 7. Mixed session. Someone was using the sewing machine to mend a pair of trousers – they’d brought their own fabric for a patch. Another person was using the 3D printer to make a small vase – it was a longer print so we left it running and they said they’d come back later. Two people came in to ask about the laser cutter – I gave them a quick overview and they booked into the September intro session. The rest were just browsing and asking questions. All good.
